bib.title: SKILLRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems), arXiv v2

question: How can LLM agents turn raw interaction experience into reusable abstract skills that co-evolve with the policy during RL, instead of storing noisy raw trajectories?
hypothesis: Effective experience transfer requires abstraction: a hierarchical skill library distilled from successes and failures, evolved during RL, beats raw-trajectory memory and plain RL.
contributions: SkillRL framework bridging raw experience and policy improvement via automatic skill discovery and recursive evolution
Hierarchical SkillBank (general + task-specific skills) distilled from successful and failed trajectories, with adaptive retrieval
Recursive skill evolution co-evolving library and GRPO policy; SOTA on ALFWorld, WebShop and 7 search QA tasks

method.summary: A teacher LLM (o3) distills base-agent rollouts into a two-level SkillBank (successes to strategy skills, failures to lessons). The student (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) is cold-start SFT'd on teacher skill-using traces, then trained with GRPO with retrieved skills in context; after each validation epoch the teacher adds skills for categories with success below a threshold.
method.task: LLM agent RL on ALFWorld, WebShop and search-augmented QA

datasets.name: ALFWorld
datasets.source: Shridhar et al. [35]; six subtask types Pick, Look, Clean, Heat, Cool, Pick2

models.name: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
models.context: max prompt 6,000 + max response 1,024 tokens in RL

other.note: teacher ablation on Tinker platform, App D.3

training.objective: Stage 1: cross-entropy SFT on teacher skill-augmented traces (Eq 6). Stage 2: GRPO with binary success reward, KL to SFT policy (Eq 9)
training.batch_size: SFT 16; RL 64 (Table 4); Section 4.1 says batch size 16, group size 8, 4 gradient accumulation steps
training.regularisation: KL loss coef 0.01; invalid action penalty coef 0.1
training.compute: inferred: about 30 h x 8 H100 per experiment
training.wall_clock: trajectory collection 3 h, skill distillation 0.5 h, cold-start SFT 2 h, RL 24 h, total ~30 h

other.note_delta: delta is used both as similarity threshold in Eq 4 (value not given) and as 0.4 evolution threshold

inference.prompting: System prompt with task, retrieved skills, history, admissible actions; reason in <think> then <action>
inference.retrieval: General skills always included; task-specific via embedding similarity above threshold, top-K=6; embedding model not stated

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of episodes with binary success

metrics.name: QA score
metrics.definition: per-dataset score, average over 7 sets (metric not defined, presumably exact match)

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no error bars or seeds (checklist: significance 'No'). Some baselines replicated from other papers (ReAct, Reflexion, RLOO, GRPO from [8]; QA baselines from [36]).

prompts.text: Analyze these failed {env_description} agent trajectories and suggest NEW skills to add. FAILED TRAJECTORIES: {failure_examples} EXISTING SKILL TITLES: {existing_titles} Generate 1-3 NEW actionable skills that would help avoid these failures. Each skill must have: skill_id, title (3-5 words), principle (1-2 sentences), when_to_apply. The skill_id should be unique and follow the pattern: "dyn_001", "dyn_002", etc. Return ONLY a JSON array of skills, no other text.

Generate 8-12 GENERAL SKILLS that apply across ALL task types. These should be: 1. Concise; 2. Actionable; 3. Transferable; 4. Failure-aware. Focus on: Navigation, object manipulation, state tracking, error recovery, and container interaction rules.
prompts.where: App C.2 Prompt B.2 (preamble and trajectory slots abridged; full in PDF)

prompts.text: Generate 10-15 GENERAL SKILLS. Focus on: Search query formulation, product selection heuristics, option configuration (size, color, etc.), constraint verification, navigation patterns, and price handling.

You are an expert agent operating in the ALFRED Embodied Environment. Your task is to: {task_description} ## Retrieved Relevant Experience {retrieved_memories} ## Current Progress ... first reason step-by-step ... enclosed within <think> </think> tags ... choose an admissible action ... within <action> </action> tags.

limits: Relies on a high-capability teacher (o3) for distillation and synthetic SFT data; at 7B self-distilled skills give only 42.5 ALFWorld (Table 5), authors call this a capability threshold.
RL pipeline is compute heavy (~30 h on 8 H100 per experiment).
Growing SkillBank may add retrieval noise; updates are periodic, not real-time.
No error bars or multiple seeds (checklist item 7: No); key baselines (GRPO, RLOO, ReAct, Reflexion) are copied from other papers.
Single base model (Qwen2.5-7B) in main tables; Kimi-K2.5 teacher ablation is a rebuttal-style add-on.
Text inconsistencies: RL batch size 16 vs 64; ablation drop 'up to 25%' / '20%' vs table; PPO cited but absent from Table 1; 10-20x compression claim vs measured ~10% prompt reduction.
